About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.
Agenda
10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
10:45 AM – Building Begins
1:00 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
4:30 PM – Closing Panel
5:00 PM – Awards, Demos & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

This is for the Engineer & Technical Builder track of our hackathon. If you're interested in learning more about the Product Manager track, check out and register at this Luma: https://luma.com/frontier-builders
What building on the Frontier is like:

-------
About Obvious:
Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!
→ Learn more at obvious.ai/events

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Request to Join

About Event

Build it with OpenAI. Validate with Kane.
Kane CLI Hack Day SF, Supported by OpenAI.
Build it with an agent. Verify it with Kane.
Your agent can write an app in minutes. On October 24 you find out if that app actually works.
We're taking over a room in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI coding agents, with support from OpenAI. Kane CLI runs on OpenAI models under the hood, so for one Saturday the models that help write your code are also the ones checking it.
$30,000+ in prizes and credits
Saturday, October 24 · San Francisco · Hosted by TestMu AI, supported by OpenAI.
Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed. Apply early.
The Challenge
Build a working app with any AI coding agent. Use Kane CLI to prove it works. Ship by 6 PM.
That's all there is to it. Build a tool, a dashboard, a game, an internal utility, a strange experiment, or the side project that's been sitting in your notes app since spring. Just follow two rules:
Kane CLI has to verify your app. At minimum, run it at demo time. The teams that win will go further and put Kane inside the agent: a hook that runs Kane on every save, an agent that reads Kane's NDJSON output and keeps fixing until the flows pass, or a spec that compiles straight into Kane flows.

Your app has to run, ship and survive a live demo. Judges want to see it working in front of them.

Come solo or bring a team of up to four. Bring your laptop and your stack. We'll cover food, coffee, credits and help on the floor.
Pick your track
Web App: The fastest route from idea to verified. Kane CLI works on web apps right out of the box.

Mobile App: Build for iOS or Android and watch Kane test it on real devices through TestMu AI's device cloud.

Wildcard: Anything goes, as long as it ships and Kane can verify it.

Special Prize, Most Innovative Use of Kane CLI: For the team that does something with Kane that we didn't see coming.

The Prizes
🥇 1st Place: Apple Vision Pro + $3,000 in OpenAI credits

🥈 2nd Place: Apple Mac mini + $2,000 in OpenAI credits

🥉 3rd Place: Apple iPad + $1,000 in OpenAI credits

Every winning team also gets:
A 1:1 with the TestMu AI founders

Design partner status, with a say in the Kane CLI roadmap

A featured post on the TestMu blog

A spot on the Kane CLI showcase

A push across TestMu and dev.to channels

Every builder walks away with
$250 in OpenAI credits

3 months of KaneAI Pro (worth $270)

A full day of food, swag, and a room full of people shipping with agents

Before you arrive
Bring the agent you already use. CLI agents, IDE agents, chat agents, MCP setups or one you built yourself all work. Install it and sign in before you get here.

Install Kane CLI and run one flow. Run npm install -g @testmuai/kane-cli and try an example from the docs. A whole room running fresh npm installs at 10:05 AM costs everyone the first hour. Your confirmation email includes a cheat sheet.

Set up your OpenAI API account. Your confirmation email will explain how to claim your $250 in credits.

FAQs
Do I have to build with OpenAI? Participants receive $250 in OpenAI API credits.
Which AI agent should I use? Whichever one you already build with. Terminal agents, IDE agents, browser agents, custom agents, MCP servers and multi-agent setups all count. Kane CLI is the one required layer, and everything above it is your call.
Which other AI tools can I use? Anything that helps you ship. There's no approved-tools list, so bring your own models, frameworks and scaffolding.
Do I need a paid Kane CLI plan? No. Every builder gets 3 months of KaneAI Pro, starting on event day.
Can I bring a project I've already started? Yes, but the Kane CLI integration has to happen on the day. At demo time, show what existed at 10 AM and what you built after that. Judges will weight the new work.
Can I work solo? Absolutely. Solo builders are welcome, and so are teams of up to four.
Do I need to know Playwright or Selenium? No. Kane CLI works in plain English: describe the flow and Kane runs it. If you know Playwright, the built-in export is a nice bonus for your writeup.
What if my project breaks during demos? Test hard before 5 PM, because submissions lock at the deadline and you can't push fixes during demos. If your app depends on a third-party service, keep a recorded run or a backup deploy ready so judges still see what you built.

About Event

Exciting hackathon with over 10k cash and credit prizes and unique theme
Please join discord for internal updates: Join Discord Server
Build an AI-native startup powered by a team of AI agents. Phase 1 is the foundation; Phase 2 is where you turn it into a functioning company.
Phase one is in Person from 10 AM to 6 PM and phase to is continuation of Phase 1 till October 11 with Demos in different location in SF having prizes for both Phases

Phase 1 — Build Day
In Person | 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM
Build 3 to 5 specialized AI agents across areas such as:
Product

Research

GTM

Sales

Marketing

Strategy

Your agents should work together through real workflows, not operate as standalone chatbots.
10:00 – 11:00 | Kickoff & Sponsor Demos
Challenge briefing

Sponsor tool demos

Team setup and Q&A

11:00 – 5:00 | Build Sprint
Build the foundation of your startup:
Identify and validate a problem

Build a simple working MVP

Create your initial AI agents

Define your business model and GTM

Prepare your demo and pitch

5:00 – 5:30 | Judging
Demo your startup and pitch to judges.
Phase 1 prizes are awarded after judging.
Completion of Phase 1 is required to continue to Phase 2.
Phase 2 — Build the AI-Native Company
October 7–11 | Online + In Person
Take your Phase 1 MVP and turn it into a functioning AI-native startup. You can build more then 5 agents now.

Build and connect your AI organization

Improve the product

Launch and test with users

Execute your GTM strategy

Phase 1: Idea → Validation → Simple MVP → Initial AI Team
Phase 2: MVP → 5+ AI Agents → Working AI Organization → Users → Investor Pitch

Request to Join

About Event

A 10-hour hackathon where you go from a plain-English spec to firmware running on a real dev board, or to a computer vision model doing real-time inference on a GPU, using CraftifAI's AI agents for hardware engineers.
📅 Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 · 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM PT
📍 San Francisco, CA
👤 Individual participation, no teams
🛠 Dev boards and sensors provided, cloud GPUs available
Why we're running this
AI coding agents changed how software gets shipped, but embedded development has barely moved. Ask a general-purpose model for an STM32 peripheral driver and you often get code that compiles cleanly, then fails on the bench because the model guessed the clock tree configuration or the pin mux. Firmware and on-device AI depend on hardware context that chat-based tools never see.
CraftifAI builds agents that work with that context. FirmGen writes, compiles, debugs and flashes firmware for ESP32 and STM32 MCUs. PipeGen turns Python CV code and ONNX models into optimized, production-ready NVIDIA DeepStream apps, benchmarked and containerized. This hackathon is your chance to put both to the test on real hardware, in a single day.
Track 1 · FirmGen: Embedded Firmware
Describe the device you want to build, whether it's a robot subsystem, a wearable or a sensor node. FirmGen plans the firmware architecture, writes the drivers and application logic, then compiles, debugs and flashes it to the board on your desk. ESP32 and STM32 dev boards and sensors are provided on site.
Bring: a laptop with a USB port.
Track 2 · PipeGen: Computer Vision & Perception
Describe what you want the camera to detect and what should happen when it does. PipeGen builds the perception stack and deploys it for real-time inference, starting from its library of benchmarked models.
Bring: Your NVIDIA GPU Laptop
Participants working with PipeGen are encouraged to bring their NVIDIA GPU-enabled laptops to the event.
We’ll also provide cloud GPU access for up to 30 participants , available on a first-come, first-served basis . This will give teams additional compute capacity for building, testing, and running their Physical AI projects during the hackathon.
If you need access to a cloud GPU, make sure to claim your spot early.
Who should apply
Firmware and embedded engineers, robotics engineers, computer vision and perception engineers, and hardware founders who want to see how far AI agents can go on real hardware.
Pre-hack office hours
On Tuesday, Oct 12, 7:00 – 9:00 PM PT , accepted hackers join a live session with the CraftifAI engineering team to set up access, test their board or cloud GPU, and get technical questions answered before the day.
Agenda
9:00 – 10:00 AM — Check-in & Hardware Pickup
10:00 – 10:30 AM — Keynote from CraftifAI founders Pratik Sharda (CEO) and Yashwant Dagar (CTO) , live from Bengaluru
10:30 – 11:45 AM — Hands-on Labs: FirmGen and PipeGen walkthroughs with the CraftifAI team
11:45 AM – 12:30 PM — Lunch & Mentor Check-ins
12:30 – 4:00 PM — Hacking & Testing, with the CraftifAI team online for technical support
4:00 – 4:30 PM — Top 5 Evaluation
4:30 – 4:45 PM — Buffer
4:45 – 5:15 PM — Live Demos & Presentations
5:15 – 6:00 PM — Closing Ceremony & Awards
6:00 – 7:00 PM — Demo Showcase & Networking
Prizes
Grand Prize: $1,000 cash + hardware prizes + OpenAI/Daytona credits
Best Perception Pipeline: Recognition for innovative use of PipeGen
Best Firmware & Edge Integration: Recognition for advanced use of FirmGen
About CraftifAI
CraftifAI is building the AI engineering layer for physical products. Every robot, drone, smart camera and industrial controller runs on firmware and perception software that engineers still write by hand, against datasheets, board revisions and silicon constraints that general-purpose AI doesn't understand. Our mission is to give hardware engineers agents that reason about the hardware the way they do, so a working device is hours away instead of months.
Orbit, our platform, brings together FirmGen for firmware, PipeGen for computer vision and AgentIQ for FPGA design.
EMBEDDED SF is the second edition of our hackathon series. The first was held at Microsoft, Bengaluru.
Spots are limited.

The Build: Hackathon
Build what’s next. Ship what matters.
Join us in San Francisco for The Build: Hackathon , a one-day gathering of engineers, AI builders, founders, product leaders, and technology professionals coming together to build real products around the challenges shaping the future of technology.
This is not just about building a prototype. It’s about taking an idea from concept to working product in one intense day.
Whether you’re building AI applications, intelligent agents, developer tools, enterprise workflows, data products, automation, or entirely new ideas, The Build is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the best builders in San Francisco, learn from industry experts, and put your work in front of experienced judges.
Event Details
When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, 14 October 2026
Where: San Francisco, CA
Who: Software Engineers, AI Engineers, Founders, Product Managers, Data Scientists, Designers, and Technology Professionals
Format: One-day, in-person hackathon
Theme: Open-ended — build something meaningful
What to Expect
An intensive one-day building experience

Build real products from idea to working prototype

Collaborate with engineers, founders, and product leaders

Mentorship from experienced industry professionals

Access to tools, platforms, APIs, and developer resources from our partners

What Can You Build?
There are no limits to what you can build.
Create an AI application, autonomous agent, developer tool, enterprise workflow, data platform, automation system, productivity product, or something completely new.
The goal is simple: identify a problem, build a solution, and ship it.
You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a problem you want to solve, a technology you want to experiment with, or simply the desire to build alongside great people.
Who Should Join?
The Build is designed for people who love creating things.
Whether you're an experienced engineer, an AI practitioner experimenting with agents, a founder validating a new idea, a product manager looking to prototype, or a developer who simply wants to spend a day building something ambitious, you're welcome.
Come to learn, build, collaborate, and ship.

Whether you’re building AI applications, intelligent agents, developer tools, enterprise workflows, data products, automation, or entirely new ideas, The Build is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the best builders in San Francisco, learn from industry experts, and put your work in front of experienced judges.

Request to Join

About Event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.
Over 36 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers, and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware, and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.
Challenge Tracks
OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis - How do you stop one compromised system from taking down an entire ship?

Piping Layout Optimization - Can algorithms find better piping and cable layouts than traditional engineering workflows?

Software-Defined Vessel - What if ships could upgrade and change missions as easily as software platforms?

Agenda
Friday, October 16
4 PM - Registration opens
5:30 PM - Welcome remarks by Fincantieri
6 PM - Reveal of challenges
7 PM - Formation of teams & hacking
8 PM - Dinner
Saturday, October 17
8 AM - Breakfast
12:30 PM - Lunch
4:00 PM - Mid-Hack Checkpoint
6:00 PM - Dinner
Sunday, October 18
8 AM - Breakfast
10:00 AM - Project submission
12:30 PM - Lunch
1:30 PM - Project Pitching
3:00 PM - Award Ceremony

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware, and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision, or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors, or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.
More Than a 36-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team (Approximate Retail Value: $1,200 USD).

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri , Mind The Bridge and Silicon Mountain .
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources, and technology expertise throughout the event.

Ecosystem Partners:

Berkeley Gateway Accelerator
Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance
Mission Applied Berkeley
Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation
SF Climate Tech Club
Bay Area Ocean Cluster
FLEETWERX
Hustle Hours
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

Full details regarding participation rules, eligibility, and data privacy can be found in our Terms and Conditions .
What to Expect
36 hours of hands-on building and prototyping.

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri.

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources.

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event.

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers.

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team.

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts.

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon , and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design, or prototyping.
Come with a team or find one at the event.
Spots are limited — register early to secure your place. Registration will close on October 15.

To help us maintain an accurate headcount, a $20 refundable deposit is required to reserve your spot. The deposit will be fully refunded upon your attendance at the event.

Who Is Bubble Lab?
Bubble Lab (YC W26) is the operating system for paid professional communities — member directory, applications, onboarding, matchmaking and engagement workflows in one place, built around Slack and compatible with Discord, WhatsApp and the rest of your stack. Communities show up juggling ~14 tools and about 20 hours a week of manual admin; Bubble Lab replaces the lot.
It's built by Selina Li and Zach Zhong , a second-time founding duo out of Cornell Tech. Selina went UPenn → quant researcher at J.P. Morgan Asset Management → CEO; Zach went UCSD CS → founding engineer at CutiePet → CTO. Before Bubble Lab they shipped gymii.ai together, an AI nutrition tracker that reached thousands of users through Cornell Tech's Spinouts program. Two people, in San Francisco, out-shipping teams many times their size.

Who is Lunatechs?
A tech-enthusiast community — find your fellow tech lunatics. Talks, workshops, meetups, hackathons; no gatekeeping, no monthly commitment. Born in Hong Kong, now 1,000+ members there, with chapters in Hong Kong and Singapore. After Shanghai the tour hits San Francisco, Dallas, Houston, Los Angeles and Palo Alto — Shanghai gets to open it.
Lunatechs is run by people who've shipped things you've used. Co-founder Hanley Leung is an engineering leader out of Apple, EA and Yahoo!. Co-founder Jason Xu built product at Google and Alibaba. Between them: decades in big tech, and years of hands-on experience working in China's tech world — this isn't a fly-in event; it's a community run by people who know Shanghai's builders are among the best anywhere.

"Europe's base in Silicon Valley." A Bay Area hub giving European startups and investors a physical and virtual foothold in the US: coworking and event space, a coliving residence, an online community, and hands-on help with market entry, customer acquisition and raising from US VCs. Led by CEO Vladimira Cincurova.

About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.
Agenda
10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
10:45 AM – Building Begins
1:00 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
4:30 PM – Closing Panel
5:00 PM – Awards, Demos & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

This is for the Engineer & Technical Builder track of our hackathon. If you're interested in learning more about the Product Manager track, check out and register at this Luma: https://luma.com/frontier-builders
What building on the Frontier is like:

-------
About Obvious:
Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!

About Event

Hey San Francisco, get ready for a startup pitch competition, investor feedback sessions, and curated networking - happening alongside TechCrunch 2026!
Join us for a high-energy evening where founders take the stage, investors share insights, and global tech leaders connect at Venture Night San Francisco .
Venture Night is part of TechEmbassy’s global event series , connecting ambitious founders, investors, and technology leaders around the world’s major tech conferences.
Expect promising startups, fast-paced pitches, direct investor feedback, and meaningful connections with people building and backing what’s next.
Our Co-hosts & Community Partners
Nazar Gulyk - tech entrepreneur and Forbes Business Council member based in San Francisco. A Stanford GSB graduate and Techstars Community Leader, he empowers early-stage founders to bring their innovative ideas to life.
Our co-hosts, Techstars Startup Weekend SF AI & Catalyst Bay , bring together the Bay Area’s AI startup community.
Techstars Startup Weekend SF AI is a 7,500-person community that brings together founders, builders, researchers, and investors through startup pitches, hackathons, and events exploring how AI is transforming health, fintech, and consumer products.
Catalyst Bay started with Techstars Startup Weekend SF hackathons. Now it's a 10,000+ person SF community running pitch nights, fireside chats, and meetups for people building and betting on AI products: founders, investors, engineers, designers, PMs, marketers, and devrels.
What to expect
🚀 Startup Pitch Competition with Prizes
10 selected startups from around the world will pitch live on stage to a panel of active investors and industry leaders.
Each founder gets 3 minutes to pitch , followed by rapid Q&A and direct jury feedback.
Expect quick pitches, real investor perspectives, and a high-energy format that keeps startups in the spotlight.
💡 Founder Feedback Session
Next up is a founder feedback session with investors and experienced startup leaders.

About Event

As AI gets more capable, so do the threats.
AI is reshaping the economics of cyberattacks: vulnerabilities can be found faster, attacks automated, and sophisticated techniques deployed at unprecedented scale.
Recent security tests also show frontier AI systems escaping controlled environments and reaching real-world systems. Yet this shift gives defenders a rare opportunity to rethink how we secure critical software, infrastructure, and digital systems.
We want to bring together developers, security engineers, ML/AI engineers, infrastructure engineers, and agent builders to tackle this head-on.

🛡️ What You’re Building For
Threat discovery · find vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and attack paths before they’re exploited

Attack intelligence · turn fragmented signals into a clear picture of what’s happening

Autonomous remediation · patch, harden, and verify fixes with minimal human intervention

Continuous defense · systems that monitor, adapt, and respond as threats evolve

🚀 AI Startup Challenge Hackathon: The Pre-Event of SF AI Summit
Get ready for the AI Startup Challenge Hackathon , an action-packed innovation sprint bringing together AI builders, founders, engineers, product leaders, and entrepreneurs at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco.
As the official pre-event of the SF AI Summit , this hackathon is designed for teams building the next generation of AI startups, products, and intelligent applications.
Whether you're building an AI agent, developer tool, enterprise solution, AI infrastructure, or an entirely new AI-native product, this is your opportunity to build, validate, demo, and compete alongside some of the most ambitious builders in the Bay Area.

When: 09:30 AM – 6:00 PM, October 20, 2026

Where: AWS Builder Loft, San Francisco, CA

Theme: AI Startups, AI Agents, Enterprise AI & AI Infrastructure

Part of: SF AI Summit

About Event

What if you could go from idea to startup in a single day?
Join founders, builders, creators, students, and entrepreneurs for an intensive one-day challenge where you’ll use Kylon and AI teammates to turn an idea into a real, launch-ready startup.
This isn’t a traditional hackathon focused on writing the most code. The goal is to build a complete business — validate a real problem, develop the product, create your AI-powered organization, and pitch your startup.
What You’ll Build
Throughout the day, your team will work through the key stages of building a startup:
Discover — Identify a meaningful problem and define your customer

Validate — Research the market and test your assumptions

Build — Create your product and working MVP

Organize — Build AI teammates to help with product, research, marketing, sales, strategy, and more

Launch — Develop your brand, landing page, business model, and go-to-market strategy

Pitch — Present your startup, product, and vision to judges and investors

Your AI Team
With Kylon, you’ll build an AI-powered organization designed around your startup.
Create the teammates you need — from AI co-founders and product managers to researchers, engineers, marketers, sales agents, and strategic advisors — and use them to accelerate your startup throughout the challenge.
Who Should Join?
Founders • Developers • Designers • Product Managers • Students • Marketers • Business Owners • Researchers • Entrepreneurs
You don’t need to be a technical expert. A strong idea, domain knowledge, creativity, and the ability to use AI effectively can be just as valuable.
What Judges Will Look For
Teams will be evaluated on:
Problem & customer validation

Market opportunity

Product quality

Business model

AI-native execution

Creativity and effectiveness of AI teammates

Go-to-market strategy

Startup potential

Quality of the final pitch and demo

The Goal
By the end of the day, you won’t just have a prototype.
You’ll have the foundation of a real AI-native startup — and the opportunity to put it in front of mentors, investors, and the broader startup community.
One day. One idea. One startup.
Build your AI-native startup with Kylon.

structuredEvent.description:
If you have registered on here, please join discord channel as well: https://discord.gg/sdEBnvwHhG

What if you could go from idea to startup in a single day?
Join founders, builders, creators, students, and entrepreneurs for an intensive one-day challenge where you’ll use Kylon and AI teammates to turn an idea into a real, launch-ready startup.
This isn’t a traditional hackathon focused on writing the most code. The goal is to build a complete business — validate a real problem, develop the product, create your AI-powered organization, and pitch your startup.
What You’ll Build
Throughout the day, your team will work through the key stages of building a startup:
Discover — Identify a meaningful problem and define your customer
Validate — Research the market and test your assumptions
Build — Create your product and working MVP
Organize — Build AI teammates to help with product, research, marketing, sales, strategy, and more
Launch — Develop your brand, landing page, business model, and go-to-market strategy
Pitch — Present your startup, product, and vision to judges and investors
Your AI Team
With Kylon, you’ll build an AI-powered organization designed around your startup.
Create the teammates you need — from AI co-founders and product managers to researchers, engineers, marketers, sales agents, and strategic advisors — and use them to accelerate your startup throughout the challenge.
Who Should Join?
Founders • Developers • Designers • Product Managers • Students • Marketers • Business Owners • Researchers • Entrepreneurs
You don’t need to be a technical expert. A strong idea, domain knowledge, creativity, and the ability to use AI effectively can be just as valuable.
What Judges Will Look For
Teams will be evaluated on:
Problem & customer validation
Market opportunity
Product quality
Business model
AI-native execution
Creativity and effectiveness of AI teammates
Go-to-market strategy
Startup potential
Quality of the final pitch and demo
The Goal
By the end of the day, you won’t just have a prototype.
You’ll have the foundation of a real AI-native startup — and the opportunity to put it in front of mentors, investors, and the broader startup community.
One day. One idea. One startup.
Build your AI-native startup with Kylon.

About Event

Build AI Agents That Own Their Inference — Powered by Akamai Cloud
What if an AI agent could control the infrastructure behind its own intelligence?
Join us on October 12, 9:30 AM–8:30 PM PT , for a full day of hands-on building with Akamai Cloud. You’ll explore Akamai Cloud’s AI compute, GPU, and inference capabilities, then use a pre-provisioned sandbox to build and run an AI agent directly from your own machine—without waiting for infrastructure access.
We’ll start with a technical workshop introducing the platform and the idea of “agents that own their inference”: giving agents greater control over where and how their models run. After lunch and networking, we’ll shift into a two-plus-hour build sprint where you’ll turn what you learned into a working prototype.
Akamai Cloud engineers and technical experts will be available throughout the day to answer questions, troubleshoot, and help bring your idea to life. We’ll close with live demos, feedback from judges, and recognition for standout projects.
Come ready to write code, experiment, and meet other builders. You don’t need a finished idea—just bring your laptop and curiosity.

Morning: Technical workshop and sandbox setup

Midday: Lunch and networking

Closing: Live demos, judging, and project recognition

Laptop and charger

Your questions and willingness to build

Request to Join

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Free 3-day Sprint for pre-seed founders. October 21 to 23, SAP Labs, Palo Alto.
Judges from Stanford, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft AI spend three days watching how your team actually works, then question you on it. You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate, built for investor conversations.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures and join Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator.
20 team spots. Applications close Oct 14
Judges
Mohammad Rasouli Phd., Researcher, AI for Private Markets, Stanford
Sajal Garg, Principal Soft Eng, Microsoft AI
Abhinav Balasubramanian, AI Lead, Nvidia
Tharun Tej Tammineni, AI Lead, Meta
What this is
Judges who lead AI at Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft AI, and Stanford spend three days watching how your team works, then question you on it. They'll push on your build, your technical claims, and how your team decides. Better here than in a pitch meeting.
You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate. Evidence you can bring to investors, not a pitch deck you rehearsed.
Two tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no customer contact yet. For founders seriously exploring a startup, including people inside companies weighing the leap.
Pre-Seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what changed, pressure-test your next move.
What you get
No cash. No trophy. Something more useful.
Teams that clear the Sprint's scoring bar earn the Street Test : 30 days back in the real world, building with no event deadline and no audience, just you and the market. It's a bar, not a ranking. Every team that clears it gets in.
Teams that finish the Street Test receive a Proving Ground report card , a scored record of how you operated across both stages. It covers three things: whether customers are pulling (Pull), whether progress held up after the event (Momentum), and whether this team fits this problem (Founder Fit). It's yours - bring it to investors, accelerators, or a cofounder you're recruiting.
A hackathon ends when the event does. This doesn't.

Wednesday, Oct 21: 9am to 8pm. Kickoff, building begins.
Thursday, Oct 22: 9am to 8pm. Full build day.
Friday, Oct 23: 9am to 4pm. Finals, live defense, deliberation, awards.
Who should apply
Pre-seed founders with live customer conversations.
Builders, product leaders, designers, and operators ready to test an idea for real.
University students: the commitment is all three days, Wednesday to Friday, 9am to close. Limited undergrad spots.

About Event

Agentic AI Hackathon at AWS Community Day Bay Area 2026
Build an agent that does real work on AWS. Two weeks. One track. Eight teams demo live on stage at AWS Community Day in front of 500+ builders. Up to $3,200 in AWS credits for the winners. First 25 teams to be formed will each get $50 AWS credits to build their ideas and bring it to life.
How it works
Register here by September 30. Every team member registers individually on this page and enters the same team name.
Build from October 1 to October 11 remotely. The top 8 submissions get a 5-minute live demo slot on October 13 at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco, judged on the spot, with winners announced at the closing session.
Who should join
Anyone building with Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents SDK, SageMaker, or any other AWS AI service. Teams of 2 to 4. Solo builders welcome; register anyway and we'll match you with a team before September 29.
The rules in brief
Work starts September 29, not before

At least two AWS services, one of them an AI service

Public GitHub repo, MIT or Apache 2.0 license

No production data, PHI, or PII

You keep your IP

Submit by October 11, 11:59 AM PT: public repo, 3-minute demo video, one-page writeup. Submission link goes out in the October 1 start announcement.
Judging: technical depth (30%), real-world usefulness (25%), responsible AI (20%), demo and communication (15%), completeness (10%). Judges score all submissions asynchronously on October 12, then re-score the 8 finalists live.
Prizes: 1st place gets $500 in AWS credits per team member (up to 4). 2nd place gets $300 per team member (up to 4). All 8 finalists get their demo featured on the AWS Community Bay Area YouTube channel.

Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026 .
Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm , Meta , GitHub , the PyTorch Foundation , and Open Intelligence Foundation , this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch —an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.
Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.
Compute Track
Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.
Mobile + XR Track
Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.
IoT Track
Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino ® VENTUNO™ Q boards , combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences. Choose from an assortment of modulinos and accessories to complete your project (available on a first come, first served basis).
To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.
Prizes
The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.
Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.
Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.

Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

The Open Intelligence Foundation is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week , a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

Founders, Inc. backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

About Event

🛑 The best teacher a student ever has is about to be an AI. Build it.
One-on-one tutoring is the highest-leverage intervention in education. Bloom's 2-sigma problem, 30 years unsolved because good tutors do not scale. AI changes that. What used to cost $80 an hour with a Stanford grad student now runs at $0.03 per student per session.
But the model is not the product. The tutor is. Which subjects. Which pedagogy. Which feedback loops. Which trust signals. Which handoffs to a real teacher when the AI hits its limits.
This weekend we build the tutors that actually teach, not just answer.
🛠️ Join our Discord for credits, team formation, and support: Join Discord Server — 1-2 Builders per team

Math, physics, chemistry, language. Depth over breadth. Show a tutor that beats generic ChatGPT in one subject specifically.

Personalization that actually adapts. Spaced repetition, Bloom's taxonomy, mastery-based progression. Show a learner outcome improved measurably.

Conversational tutors that hear, see, and respond. Screen-share tutoring. Oral exam prep. Whiteboard-native math.
📊 Track 4 · Assessment & Feedback
Essay grading, oral exams, code review. Fast, calibrated, humane feedback that a student trusts.

Request to Join

About Event

Tech Week Prelaunch Event - Physical AI for Anyone | Bring Your Impossible Idea
That product you keep imagining — and quietly talking yourself out of — belongs in the room this Thursday.
You know the one. The idea that shows up in the shower. On the drive home. In that 1 a.m. Notes app draft you never send anyone because… hardware feels too hard, too expensive, too “not for people like me.”
What if that story is wrong?
This Thursday, bring your impossible idea anyway. The wild one. The tender one. The one that makes your friends say “that would be so cool” and then change the subject. We’re building a room where imagination doesn’t get shut down — it gets built.
What it's about
Physical AI for Anyone is 2 hours of creative voltage: founders, dreamers, and first-timers turning something you can only picture in your head into something the physical world can start to hold.
You’ll hear from hardware founders who once stood exactly where you are — scared, excited, unsure — and still shipped something real. Then you’ll open your laptop and chase your idea with Vlight AI: explore how it could look, feel, come apart, get made. Not a lecture. A leap.
There will be laughter. There will be “wait, that actually works?” moments. There will be a one-minute pitch where your idea gets to breathe in front of people who get it. And when you walk out, you won’t just have notes — you’ll have proof that you started.
If you’ve ever felt that little ache of “I wish I could make this,” this night is for that ache.
Who it's for
For the founder with no hardware background and a full heart. For the designer tired of living only on screens. For the student with an impossible sketch. For anyone who’s ever said “someone should invent this” — and secretly meant you.
You don’t need credentials. You need courage for one afternoon. If you can feel the idea, you’re already in.
What you get
Permission to take your impossible idea seriously — in public

A room buzzing with people who want to build, not just talk

Vlight AI credits + humans beside you when you get stuck

Honest stories from 1–2 hardware founders who made the leap

Sixty seconds on stage. A vote. A rush. A winner — and a story you’ll want to tell

Llight snacks, coffee/water/soft drinks, and warmth from Plug and Play That rare high: I didn’t just dream it. I began it.

About Event

AI is moving faster than most security programs can keep up with — agentic tools, MCP servers, and AI-generated code are shipping into production every day, often outrunning the guardrails meant to protect them. This hackathon brings developers and security practitioners together to get hands-on with the skills defining the new discipline of AI Security Engineering. Working in teams, participants will tackle real-world AI security challenges spanning securing MCP servers and agent skills against tool poisoning and supply-chain attacks, and hardening vibe-coded applications.
Whether you're a developer curious about securing AI-powered apps or a security specialist looking to apply your skills to LLMs and agents, you'll leave with practical, portfolio-ready experience — and the kind of muscle memory that only comes from breaking (and fixing) real systems. No prior AI security experience required — just a builder's mindset and curiosity about where AI meets attack surface.

Snyk
Snyk is a developer-first cybersecurity platform that helps teams build fast without compromising on security. As developers rely heavily on AI to write code at unprecedented speeds, Snyk continuously scans and secures application code, open-source dependencies, containers, and cloud environments right within the developer’s workflow. For an AI hackathon, it matters because shipping code quickly with AI generators or autonomous agents also means shipping security risks at machine speed. Snyk acts as an intelligent security layer, catching vulnerabilities and automatically applying verified fixes in real time—allowing builders to ship ambitious AI projects safely and with complete confidence.

About Event

The AI Conference Hack Day is where 350 builders unite to do something that was impossible a year ago: build a working product — a real business — in a single day.
This isn't a hackathon in the old sense. No throwaway demos, no clever prototypes that die the next day. The AI Conference Hack Day brings together 350 builders, engineers, product and business minds to ship something real. Something that runs. Something a customers will actually use — and maybe pay for before the day is out.
For one day, the usual excuses disappear. You don't need a team of fifty. You don't need a year of runway. You don't need permission. What used to be a roadmap is now an afternoon. What used to be a funding round is now a focused day of work and the will to ship.
That's not hype. It's where the frontier actually is right now.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts the first billion-dollar company with a single human employee will arrive as soon as 2026 —
Every one of those companies has a day zero. This is where yours could begin.
Here's how it works. You'll have a single day to take an idea from nothing to a working product. You'll build alongside the sharpest practitioners in applied AI — the engineers, ML leads, and founders who already live at the edge of what these tools can do. Mentors will be in the room. The energy will be unlike anything else at the conference. And at the end of the day, prizes go to the teams who didn't just build something interesting, but built something real.
The top prize is the one that matters most. The best product team won't just take home recognition — they'll take the main stage at The AI Conference the very next day to pitch a panel of top venture capitalists. That's the kind of room most founders wait years to get into. You could earn your seat in twenty-four hours.
This is the bet we're making: that the next great company won't be announced in a press release. It'll be built in a room full of people who decided not to wait. It'll start as a half-formed idea on Day ZERØ and walk out as something real.
The era of the solo builder, the tiny team that punches a hundred times above its weight, the one-person company — it's not coming someday. It's starting now, and it's starting here.
This is your shot.
Don't miss it.

Request to Join

About Event

If you have registered on here, please join discord channel as well: Join Discord Server
You bring the idea. Build the AI that makes it happen.
The Challenge
Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2–4 co-founders, combining humans and AI.
Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder. You decide the rest—including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together.
AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs.
The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team—from idea to execution to a shipped product.
Prizes
Build the Product challenge using AdaL prize: +1 month AdaL pro for the winners
Using AdaL, build and ship a functional app or MVP for a real-world problem. Your product should be something real people can use and should demonstrate how your human–AI founding team turns an idea into a working company.
The focus is on execution: build a useful product, validate it with real users, and show what your AI co-founder contributed to the journey from idea to launch.
Ask The W think Before You Build Challenge: Prizes: Gift cards for best context, most bugs found and an opportunity to build with the founder. More details: https://askthew.com/hackathon

The fastest way to ship is to avoid building the wrong thing.

Use Ask The W to gather the right context, question assumptions and get clear on what should be built before writing code. Understand first. Build second.
Tenki code review challenge: 1000 Tenki credits for winner
Use Tenki to sandbox, test, and review your project’s code. Identify bugs and issues in AI-generated code, improve the implementation, and demonstrate how your team builds, reviews, fixes, and ships reliable software.

Our sponsors provide the technology and infrastructure you'll use to turn your ideas into working companies.
AdaL
AdaL is automation-first agent harness and coding companion. While any coding agent can build, AdaL uniquely turns your codebase into go-to-market execution, helping you ship faster from development to launch.. Learn more at adalagent.ai.
AdaL code: COFOUNDERHACKATHON-K4CG for 1 month of AdaL Pro free, or 30% off Max and Max+. Redeem at adalagent.ai by 12 Oct.
AdaL technical support on Discord: Join Discord Server

Nebius provides AI-focused cloud infrastructure and computing resources designed to help teams build, train, and run modern AI applications and workloads.

Tenki provides developer infrastructure at tenki.cloud, including sandboxes, code review, and code runners to help teams safely build, test, and iterate on their products.

100+ AI models, composable skills, and deployable agents unified under one API. Build, monetize, and scale autonomous workflows with pay-per-call simplicity at Aisa.com

Ask the W helps you figure out what is worth building with AI. It helps identify good ideas, tasks that can be handled by agents, places where human judgment is needed, and the next steps to take.

Build It: Launch the Business
Turn your idea into a launch-ready business. Your AI co-founder helps with research, permits, costs, suppliers, branding, operations, and the launch plan.

Prepare your company to raise funding. Your AI co-founder researches investors, finds the right fit, builds fundraising materials, and helps manage outreach.

Get your first customers. Your AI co-founder identifies prospects, researches them, creates personalized outreach, and supports the sales process.

Build a repeatable growth engine. Your AI co-founder helps define your audience, develop positioning, test channels, run experiments, and measure results.

About Event

Win up to $5M in Seed Funding* | September 27th, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM PT
In partnership with "Girls into VC" @ UC Berkeley
Join us for an elite hackathon where you'll build cutting-edge projects with Google Gemini and earn 30-minute pitch meetings with top-tier VCs.
🏆 The Prize
Top teams will be judged by representatives from Google, Berkeley, Stanford, and multiple venture capital funds.
Grand Prize — VC Pitch Access: A 30-minute private pitch meeting with selected funds from our judging panel — VCs writing $500K–$5M seed checks. Pitch your hackathon project or your existing startup.
Google AI Studio Track (sponsored by DeepMind):
In-Person: share of $15K in GCP credits

Online: share of $5K in GCP credits

*Investment not guaranteed. The prize is pitch access only — winning teams gain meeting access but must earn investment through their pitch and business fundamentals.
📅 Event Schedule
10:00 AM — Registration & Breakfast: light refreshments and networking with fellow builders

10:30 AM — Opening Ceremony & Rules Briefing: official rules and competition format

11:30 AM — Hacking Begins: 3-hour build sprint

2:30 PM — Submission Deadline (hard stop): all submissions must be in

2:30 PM — Late Lunch: sandwiches, beverages, and networking

3:30 PM — Semi-Finalists Announced: top teams selected for live pitches

🌐 Online Track
Can't make it to campus? We've added an Online Track for remote participants:
No live streaming or video conferencing — work on your own schedule

Submission deadline: end of day, September 27

Same deliverables as in-person participants

Judging based on traction — same conditions as Phase 2 (7-day social engagement tracking)

Prize pool: $5K in GCP credits

VC pitch access for top submissions

Build with Gemini, ship a prototype, post your demo, and let your network do the talking. Top submissions get 30-minute meetings with funds.
📋 Submission Requirements
All projects must use the Google Gemini model. Each team must submit the following by 2:30 PM sharp:
One-Pager for the team — Short plain text describing your team and your pedigree

One-Pager for the idea — Short plain text describing your idea and prototype

Hosted Prototype — Working demo link (via Google AI Studio & Google Cloud Run)

2-Minute Video — Team introduction and elevator pitch

1-Minute Video — Prototype demo (Playcast)

Code Repository — Link via Google AI Studio sharing

Data Usage & Judging Consent: By submitting your prototype Playcast, you authorize organizers to use your submission in paid social ads (e.g., Facebook). Real-world performance metrics (CPM, CTR, CPC, etc.) will be collected and used as core market validation data for Phase 2 (post-event) judging. You may opt out by notifying organizers prior to submission; data sharing with sponsors and investors is a condition of participation.
⚖️ Judging Criteria
Technical Feasibility — Does it actually work?

Innovation & Novelty — Is the approach creative or clever?

Real-World Applicability — Would people genuinely use it?

Market Potential & Fundability — Could this become venture-backable?

Go-to-Market Traction — Social engagement on your demo video (likes, shares, views)

Social Engagement Component: Your demo YouTube video must be shared publicly. Engagement counts toward your score:
Phase 1 — Tracked during the hackathon (5:00 PM cutoff)

Phase 2 — Continued tracking for 2 weeks post-event (viral reach + Playcast metrics)

About Event

AI Commerce Gallery — ZooWork × AI Valley
What does the next generation of AI-powered commerce look like?
ZooWork and AI Valley are bringing together builders, founders, engineers, designers, and commerce leaders for AI Commerce Gallery — a curated one-day hackathon and interactive showcase for products pushing commerce forward.
On October 3rd, AI Commerce Gallery takes over The Walt Disney Family Museum in San Francisco for a full day of building, demos, and exploration.
Teams will build throughout the day in the Diane Disney Miller Exhibition Hall before the evening program moves into the Main Museum, with presentations in the Theater and Lower Lobby and private access to the Museum’s Main Galleries from 7:30–9 PM.

Teams will build AI-powered products across:
E-commerce & storefront experiences

Merchant operations, inventory, fulfillment & payments

Restaurants, retail, POS & physical commerce

AI agents, MCP integrations & workflow automation

The strongest projects will take the stage in The Walt Disney Family Museum’s Theater , bringing a day of bold ideas to life in a place built to celebrate imagination.
Then celebrate the winners, meet fellow builders, and enjoy private access to the Museum’s Main Galleries from 6–9 PM — ending the day with a little Disney magic.

Best Use of ZooWork
People’s Choice

Celebrate the winners and connect with builders, partners, judges, investors, and industry guests.
7:30–9:00 PM — Private Main Galleries Access 🏰

9:00 PM — Event Closing
The evening concludes and the venue closes.
Come build — or come see — what the next generation of AI-powered commerce looks like.
ZooWork — The AI agent delivery platform for FDEs and domain experts. Build, deploy, and deliver production-ready AI agents to your team or clients in minutes—with Agent Builder, Agent Runtime, model gateway, data, and integrations all in one place. ZooWork turns your expertise into repeatable AI solutions that run inside real business operations, connected to the tools your teams already use. Learn more at zoowork.ai .

Moss ( moss.dev ) is a real-time semantic search engine that gives AI agents sub-10ms retrieval without the latency and infrastructure overhead of traditional vector databases.

Entire is building the next agentic Git forge. Store your prompts, output, tool calls, and more alongside your code in Git, perform rapid-fast Git operations on their distributed Git network, and save token usage on their human-agent developer platform.

Tavily helps AI agents access up-to-date information from the web. Its search, extraction, and crawling APIs let developers build applications that research topics, gather data, and turn web content into useful answers.

Novita AI is an AI infrastructure platform for builders. It offers access to AI models through a single API, along with GPU compute for training and inference and secure runtimes for AI agents. Developers can start with serverless APIs and scale to dedicated endpoints or GPU clusters as their needs grow.

BAND helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done.

AI Valley is a community rooted in supporting exceptional first generation builders, founders, and creators. We curate environments where ambitious people meet collaborators, mentors, and opportunities through hackathons, workshops, and intimate gatherings across AI, tech, and the arts. If you care about who you build with as much as what you build, this is your place.

About Event

Women Build Oakland: From Idea to App in One Day
Have an idea for an app, website, or digital tool—but not sure how to build it?
Women Build Oakland is a free, beginner-friendly AI buildathon designed to help women turn ideas into working digital products in just one day.
Presented by CoCo Noir Labs , this hands-on event will bring together 50 women founders, professionals, creatives, students, small-business owners, community leaders, and aspiring technology builders.
No previous coding experience is required.
Participants will join small teams of two to four women and work together to build one shared app, website, or digital tool that addresses a real business or community challenge. You can contribute through business strategy, research, project management, design, marketing, storytelling, prompting, testing, coding, or presenting.
What to Expect
During the event, participants will:
Learn the basics of AI-powered vibe coding

See how an idea can become a working digital product

Meet women with different professional and creative skills

Form a team around a shared idea or challenge

Build a functional prototype with support from mentors

Present the completed project to a panel of judges

Compete for prizes and special recognition

Teams may build solutions related to:
Women’s economic opportunity and entrepreneurship

Small-business and hospitality innovation

Health, wellness, caregiving, and safety

Workforce development and education

Community and public services

Oakland’s culture and creative economy

Who Should Apply
This event is for women and women-identifying adults who are curious about AI, technology, entrepreneurship, or solving meaningful problems.
You may be a:
First-time AI builder

Founder or small-business owner

Working professional or executive

Creative or community leader

Student or career changer

Designer, product manager, or developer

Beginners are encouraged to apply. You do not need to arrive with an idea or have technical experience. You only need to be ready to learn, collaborate, and build.
Registration Details
Participation is free

Space is limited to 50 builders

Registration is application-based

Submitting an application does not guarantee acceptance

Accepted participants must be available for the full program from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Participants should bring a laptop and charger

Lunch, refreshments, mentorship, and event materials will be provided

Come with an idea or simply come ready to collaborate. By the end of the day, you will have helped create a real digital product and gained the confidence to continue building with AI.
Presented and produced by CoCo Noir Labs
The event is designed to use Lovable as the primary AI app-building platform, subject to approval through Lovable’s Community Events program.
This event has been submitted for inclusion in Oakland Tech Week 2026 and is pending final confirmation.

About Event

Mission Applied: Maritime Dual-Use Announcement Mixer
Mission Applied is the new partnership between Berkeley Gateway Accelerator and the Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance (BISG). BISG does the policy and translation work: analysis, recommendations, convening. Mission Applied is the action arm, the piece that takes capability out of the labs and classrooms and turns it into companies and scalable solutions. If you've got a concept, a research thread, or a company in national security or dual-use tech, this is who you want to know.
Our first move: bringing Fincantieri's engineering challenges to Berkeley.

The evening

An informal mixer at BGA. Food, drinks, and a room full of people working on hard problems in defense and dual-use tech.

You'll hear from Mission Applied on what we're doing and where we're headed, from Mind the Bridge and Fincantieri on the October hackathon, and from mentors and judges pulled from the defense innovation ecosystem, including active-duty Navy leadership working on emerging tech acquisition.

Then we'll get out of the way and let you talk to each other.

The hackathon we're announcing

Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon, October 16-18 in San Francisco. Fincantieri builds the Italian Navy's submarines, the world's largest cruise ships, and the US Coast Guard's Constellation-class frigates. Their engineers wrote the problem statements themselves.

Three tracks: OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis, Piping Layout Optimization, and Software-Defined Vessel. Qualcomm and Arduino hardware on hand. Standout concepts get mentorship from Fincantieri's expert network and a real path toward application inside the company.

We'll walk through the tracks, the hardware, and what a strong team looks like, so you show up in October ready to build instead of ready to read.

Who should be here

Students, founders, engineers, researchers, and anyone curious about where deep tech meets national security. Undergrads and grad students from across campus, plus NPS, UCSD, and the community colleges around the East Bay. No maritime background required.

Come solo or bring your team.

Hosted by Mission Applied: Berkeley Gateway Accelerator × Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance, with Mind the Bridge and Fincantieri.

For SF Tech Week, BuilderBase, Women in AI, and AI Collective are bringing builders together at Frontier Tower for a full day of building, testing, and live demos.
The challenge
Build an AI product that becomes more useful because it combines more than one model, provider, agent, or modality. Use the right system for each job: reasoning, code, vision, voice, long context, fast inference, or whatever your product needs.
Build something a real person would use. By the end of the day, show what it does, why one model would not have been enough, and what the combination unlocks.

Engineers, AI practitioners, designers, and technical founders who want to build something real in a day. No prior hackathon experience required. Bring a laptop, a problem you care about, or the willingness to join a team and start building.

Anbaric

Base44

Prelint
Your AI makes decisions. Prelint keeps every decision reviewed, recorded, and traceable. Every pull request gets a 20-second decision review.
Swytchcode
Legacy APIs and AI agents don't blend. Swytchcode gives agents the implementation knowledge these APIs never documented, then governs every action that runs.
Community Partners
Women in AI

About Event

What’s actually working for AI products right now?
Hosted by Catalyst Bay , AScaleX , and Brex
Most AI events are vendors talking about their own product. This one is the people responsible for growth at AI companies talking about what actually moved numbers.
A panel, a round table, and a long happy hour. 80 people · 40 founders + 40 GTM leaders , so you will actually talk to everyone.
The panel: Going to market when the category is contested, and nobody has won it yet. How to find demand before you have anything to sell. What positioning survives contact with real buyers. How to pick first customers for distribution rather than revenue.
Speakers :
Ravish Agrawal, Head of Growth Marketing, Gamma - Ravish leads growth marketing at Gamma. Before Gamma he spent five years as co-founder and CEO of Able, a VC-backed edtech app that grew to three million users before he exited.

Mada Seghete, Co-founder, Upside - Mada is the co-founder and CEO of Upside, a revenue attribution and intelligence platform for B2B companies. Before that, she co-founded Branch and built Mobile Growth, a community of 22,000+ mobile marketers and app developers. She co-hosts the Future of Marketing podcast.

Juliana Chyzhova, Head of Marketing, AGI, Inc.

The round tables: An open conversation around the GTM challenges people in the room are working through right now. Bring a question, compare approaches, and hear how other founders and operators are thinking about demand, positioning, customers, and distribution.
Happy hour: Food and drinks, and the part of the evening where the useful conversations happen.
Who this is for
GTM leads and heads of growth at AI companies

Founders still running go-to-market themselves

First marketing and sales hires at AI startups

Investors who spend their time on portfolio distribution

What you leave with: A positioning read on your own product from people who have done it. Two or three tactics you can run next week. And a short list of people worth following up with.

Tool-call and MCP reliability

Arrive with one agent problem, workflow, or use case.

Meet with builders and developer-tool experts at focused clinic stations.

Leave with a clear diagnosis and next-step plan.

Share fixes and lessons with the room during a short live wrap-up.

About Event

Jev is a new kind of model from TypeSafe AI. It takes unstructured context and returns typed, probabilistic decisions that software can act on.
Using Jev well changes how you design workflows. You have to decide which judgments belong to the model, how to frame those decisions, and when the result should trigger an action, human review, or escalation. The fastest way to develop that instinct, or understand the “Jevability” of a problem, is to build.
Join us at the PromptQL office on Tuesday, September 29, from 4–7 p.m. PT for a hands-on evening exploring what becomes possible when decisions get fast, structured, and cheap.
We’ll start with a lightning session dissecting the architecture of four or five real systems built with Jev, and show off some of the best builds from the previous session. We’ll look at patterns such as routing work, selecting from existing options, ranking evidence, verifying agent output, and turning confidence into reliable control flow.
Then we’ll hack.
Bring a workflow, product idea, or recurring judgment you want to rebuild. You’ll leave with a working prototype, a sharper sense of where Jev fits, and practical patterns you can reuse in future systems.
Schedule
4:00 PM: Doors open and introductions
4:15 PM: Jev architecture lightning talks
5:00 PM: Hackathon
6:30 PM: Demos and discussion
7:00 PM: Wrap
No Jev or app-building experience is needed. Engineers, founders, product builders, and anyone curious about decision-driven automation are welcome.
This is a small, hands-on gathering hosted by PromptQL. Come ready to build. Dinner will be provided.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
